<description>
{
 "summary": "Validates `CFeeRate` values during deserialization by throwing a deserialization failure if the stream contains values that constructors cannot produce. Specifically, it rejects negative sizes and zero sizes paired with non-zero fees.",
 "problem": "`CFeeRate` deserialization reads raw fee and size values without the normalization and checks enforced by its constructors. If a malformed feerate with a negative size is unpacked, it causes `FeeFrac::EvaluateFee` to fail an `Assume` assertion in debug builds or compute wrong fee amounts in release builds; zero size with non-zero fee compares as an infinite feerate. While nothing on master deserializes `CFeeRate` today, the upcoming IPC chain interface in #29409 passes feerates across process boundaries as serialized data.",
 "evidence": [
  "Discovered through fuzzing/audit by Project Loupe and reported by Greg Sanders (description, commit message)",
  "Author notes: 'With the UnstableChain IPC interface from #29409 merged, an IPC client could make bitcoin-node hit an Assume failure (debug builds) or compute wrong fees (release builds)' (description)"
 ],

<category name="mempool" title="Mempool and policy">
## Covers

Which unconfirmed transactions the node accepts, keeps, and relays:
standardness and policy rules, replacement rules, package acceptance
and relay, mempool data structures and limits, eviction, fee
estimation, and the cluster mempool project. The Mempool and TX fees
and policy labels are a strong prior.

Not mempool: consensus validity (validation); block template
construction (mining); the p2p messages that carry transactions (p2p).

## What matters here

Denial-of-service and pinning resistance first: policy is the node's
defense against transactions designed to waste resources or to block
legitimate replacements, and second-layer protocols depend on it. Then
correctness of acceptance and replacement rules against their stated
specifications, since wallets and Lightning implementations build on
them. Then progress on the cluster mempool project and the improvements
it unblocks. Then fee estimation accuracy, which every wallet user
feels. Then memory and CPU behavior under load.

Policy changes with a written rationale and downstream demand rank
above local tidy-ups.
